title: Bystander questions — 2025 guidelines
note: Answer cards for the offline assistant. RULE: every card that makes a clinical claim carries a source id from assets/protocols/sources.json and the text that claim rests on. quoteKind is 'verbatim' when the quote was transcribed character-for-character from the source; a 'paraphrase' card MUST be verified:false, and a test enforces that. Cards of kind coverageGap and meta make no clinical claim at all — they say what Mayday does not know and hand the caller to a dispatcher.

ask: they collapsed and are not breathing
i think they are in cardiac arrest
they collapsed and are not responsive
they are limp and not breathing
cards.display: Start CPR. Get someone to call 911, then push hard and fast in the centre of the chest.
cards.speech: Start C P R. Point at someone and tell them to call nine one one. Then push hard and fast in the centre of the chest. I will count the beat for you.
cards.quote: The No-No-Go framework is reiterated as an effective method for recognizing OHCA.

ask: they are making a snoring noise
they took a breath should i stop
cards.display: Gasping is not breathing. Treat it as cardiac arrest and keep going.
cards.speech: Gasping is not breathing. Treat this as cardiac arrest. Keep pushing.
cards.quote: The No-No-Go framework is reiterated as an effective method for recognizing OHCA.

ask: what rate should i be doing
cards.display: 100 to 120 pushes a minute, about 5 to 6 cm deep, letting the chest come all the way back up. Follow the beat — Mayday measures your rate and will not pretend to measure your depth.
cards.speech: A hundred to a hundred and twenty pushes a minute. Follow the beat. Push down about two inches and let the chest come all the way back up.
cards.quote: Chest compressions at a rate of 100 to 120 per minute to a depth of at least 2 inches (5 cm) but not greater than 2.4 inches (6 cm) for an average adult, allowing full chest recoil.
cards.verificationNote: The primary PDF is behind a Cloudflare challenge that refuses automated fetches. These are long-standing values carried forward from 2020 and are not listed among the 2025 changes, but they have not yet been read off the primary document.

ask: where do i put my hands
cards.display: Heel of one hand on the centre of the chest, on the lower half of the breastbone. Other hand on top. Lock your elbows.
cards.speech: Heel of one hand on the centre of the chest. Other hand on top. Lock your elbows.
cards.quote: Hand placement on the lower half of the sternum for adult chest compressions.
cards.verificationNote: Same blocked primary source as the compression rate. Confirm before relying on it.

ask: can i do cpr on a couch
should i move them to the floor
cards.display: Get them onto the floor. Compressions into a mattress or a sofa do not reach the heart.
cards.speech: Get them flat on the floor. Not a bed. Kneel beside them.
cards.quote: For adult cardiac arrest, rescuers should perform chest compressions with the patient on a firm surface and with the patient's torso at approximately the level of the rescuer's knees.

ask: do i do mouth to mouth
do i have to put my mouth on theirs
cards.display: For an adult, hands-only is what a dispatcher will coach: no breaths, just keep pushing. Children are different and need breaths — Mayday does not cover children yet.
cards.speech: For an adult, hands only. No breaths. Just keep pushing.
cards.quote: Telecommunicator CPR: Hands-Only CPR for adults; conventional CPR with breaths for children.
cards.verificationNote: PARAPHRASE, not a transcription. The 2025 Highlights split telecommunicator CPR by age; the exact wording has not been transcribed from the primary document. Confirm before relying on it.

ask: how long do i keep going
someone else wants to take over
cards.display: Keep going until they wake up or until EMS takes over. If anyone else can push, swap about every 2 minutes — Mayday will prompt you.
cards.speech: Keep going until they wake up, or until the paramedics take over. If someone else can push, swap over. I will tell you when.
cards.quote: Rescuers should switch compressors approximately every 2 minutes to avoid a decline in compression quality from fatigue.
cards.verificationNote: PARAPHRASE of the long-standing 2-minute rescuer-swap guidance. Same blocked primary source. Confirm before relying on it.

ask: how do i use a defibrillator
should i go and get the aed
do i need to know how to use it
cards.display: Turn it on and do exactly what it says — it talks you through it. Do not stop compressions to go looking for one; only stop if somebody hands it to you.
cards.speech: Turn it on and do what it says. It talks you through it. Do not stop pushing to go and look for one.

ask: do i have to take her bra off
cards.display: Bare the chest, but you can move a bra aside rather than remove it. This was made explicit in 2025 because women are defibrillated far less often than men.
cards.speech: Bare the chest. You can move a bra aside. You do not have to take it off.
cards.quote: When placing pads for defibrillation for an adult in cardiac arrest, it might be reasonable to adjust the position of a bra instead of removing it.

ask: something is stuck in their throat
it went down the wrong way
what do i do for choking
cards.display: Five back blows between the shoulder blades, then five abdominal thrusts. Repeat until it clears. Back blows first is the 2025 change — most apps still say thrusts first.
cards.speech: Five back blows between the shoulder blades. Then five thrusts. Keep repeating until it comes out.
cards.quote: Start repeated cycles of 5 back blows (slaps), followed by 5 abdominal thrusts

ask: should i hit them if they can cough
do i still do back blows if they can cough
cards.display: A strong cough means the airway is still partly open. Do not hit them, do not reach into the mouth. Stay with them and watch for the cough going quiet.
cards.speech: Let them cough. Do not hit them. Do not reach into their mouth. Stay with them and watch.
cards.quote: Encourage cough. Continue to check for signs of severe FBAO.

ask: how do i know if it is serious
what are the signs of severe choking
cards.display: Severe means: weak or no cough, cannot speak, colour changing, going vague, or no breathing at all. Any of those and you start back blows now.
cards.speech: If they cannot cough, cannot speak, are changing colour, or are going limp, this is severe. Start back blows now.
cards.quote: Check for signs of severe FBAO: Weak or absence of cough / Unable to speak / Change in colour (cyanosis) / Altered mental status / Apnea

ask: i cannot get my arms around them
they are too big to reach around
where do i put my fist if she is pregnant
cards.display: Use five chest thrusts instead of abdominal thrusts — fist on the breastbone, pull straight back.
cards.speech: Use chest thrusts instead. Fist on the breastbone. Pull straight back. Not on the belly.
cards.quote: For patients in the late stages of pregnancy, or when the rescuer is unable to encircle the patient's abdomen, 5 chest thrusts should be used instead.

ask: they collapsed and something is still stuck
what if they stop being awake
cards.display: Lower them to the floor and start CPR. Check the mouth for anything you can see before any breath.
cards.speech: Lower them to the floor. We are starting C P R now.
cards.quote: Start CPR until advanced care arrives; refer to adult BLS algorithm. Start with compressions. Check for visible object in mouth before giving breaths.

ask: it came out are they okay
do they still need a doctor
it is clear now what next
cards.display: Stay with them and keep watching their breathing. They still need to be seen by a doctor — abdominal thrusts can injure organs.
cards.speech: Good. Stay with them. They still need to see a doctor, even now. Keep watching their breathing.
cards.quote: If object is expelled, continue to monitor until advanced care arrives.

ask: do i call before i start
how do i get help coming
cards.display: Point at one person and say it to them by description: YOU in the blue coat — call 911, put it on speaker. Naming somebody is what turns a crowd into help.
cards.speech: Point at one person. Say: you. Call nine one one and put it on speaker.

ask: there is no one to help
cards.display: Call 911 yourself, speaker on, phone on the floor beside you — then keep going. While you are on the call the phone cannot hear you, so Mayday switches to the big on-screen step and tap-to-advance.
cards.speech: Call nine one one yourself. Speaker on. Put the phone down beside you and keep going. While you are on the call I cannot hear you, so tap the screen for the next step.

ask: is it safe to go in
should i move them out of the road
cards.display: Check the scene before you touch anyone. Traffic, fire, wires, water. You cannot help anyone if you become the second patient.
cards.speech: Check it is safe first. Traffic. Fire. Wires. Water. You cannot help if you are hurt.

ask: how do i do cpr on a kid
cards.display: This build only covers adults. Call 911 now and let the dispatcher coach you — the technique for a child or an infant is genuinely different, and the 2025 guidelines changed it. Do not copy the adult steps.
cards.speech: This version only covers adults. Call nine one one now. The dispatcher will talk you through it. Do not copy the adult steps for a child.

cards.display: Severe bleeding is not in this build yet. Call 911 now — the dispatcher will talk you through pressure and packing.
cards.speech: Severe bleeding is not in this version yet. Call nine one one now. The dispatcher will talk you through it.

ask: where do i use an epipen
cards.display: Anaphylaxis is not in this build yet. Call 911 now. If they have their own adrenaline auto-injector, tell the dispatcher — they will direct you.
cards.speech: Allergic reactions are not in this version yet. Call nine one one now and tell them what is happening.

ask: they took something and stopped breathing
cards.display: Opioid emergencies are not in this build yet. Call 911 now. If they are not breathing at all, say exactly that — an opioid arrest needs breaths, not hands-only, and the dispatcher will coach it.
cards.speech: Overdose is not in this version yet. Call nine one one now and tell them they are not breathing.

cards.display: Seizures are not in this build yet. Call 911 now and let the dispatcher coach you.
cards.speech: Seizures are not in this version yet. Call nine one one now.

ask: i think it is a stroke
i think it is a heart attack
cards.display: Stroke and heart attack are not in this build yet. Call 911 now — for both of these, how fast the ambulance is called is the thing that matters most.
cards.speech: That is not in this version yet. Call nine one one right now. Getting the ambulance moving is the most important thing.

ask: they were pulled out of the water
cards.display: That is not in this build yet. Call 911 now and describe exactly what you can see.
cards.speech: That is not in this version yet. Call nine one one and describe what you can see.

cards.display: I coach adult CPR and adult choking, out loud, with no signal and no account. Ask me anything about either and I will answer from the 2025 guidelines and show you the line I got it from. Anything I do not cover, I will say so and tell you to call 911.
cards.speech: I can coach you through adult C P R and adult choking. Ask me anything about either one. If I do not know something, I will tell you to call nine one one instead of guessing.

cards.display: No. Every line comes from the 2025 American Heart Association guidelines and every screen shows you the exact text it came from. Nothing here is written by a language model. It is not a substitute for training or for a dispatcher.
cards.speech: No, I am not a doctor. Everything I say comes from the twenty twenty five guidelines, and the screen shows you the exact line it came from. Call nine one one as well.

ask: will this work in a basement
cards.display: Yes. Everything — the protocols, the voice, the search — runs on the phone. There is no network call anywhere in the app.
cards.speech: Yes. Everything runs on the phone. It works with no signal at all.
